sourceRefs.locator: 22 October 2006. Ballot question, voting and turnout tables and project footnote. 705,284 yes, 201,105 no, 9,967 blank and 7,673 invalid; 924,029 ballots, 2,132,842 registered. The printed 76.3% uses all ballots. The yes/no subtotal of 906,389 gives 77.8% yes.

Title XV, Chapter 1, Article 325, first, third and fourth paragraphs. A proposal for a third set of locks requires executive and legislative approval, then a national referendum at least three months after legislative approval.

24 April 2006. Section 1, p. 3 and fig. 1, two existing lanes, new locks at both ends, channels and maximum lake level. Section 5.6, pp. 47–48, fig. 32 and note 78, gravity, three basins per chamber, 60% reuse within the new system and projected 7% less water per transit than the old locks. Section 7, p. 53, proposal using existing reservoirs.

Report RL30981, updated 16 November 2006, pp. CRS-15–16, “Canal Expansion Project”. Torrijos on revenue for social programmes and the Coordinadora Campesina Contra los Embalses on the risk of displacement. These are arguments put forward during the campaign.
Opening three paragraphs. Identifies the flag site outside the Administration Building and distinguishes the anniversary ceremony of 2019 from the transfer at noon on 31 December 1999.

The Canal Record, vol. V, no. 15, 6 December 1911, pp. 120–121. First column on the expected removal of the railway and dwellings already being taken down. The entries for Gatun, Bohio and Frijoles list the produce trade, housing, school and shops, 1908 counts and the burial of old Gatun under the dam. The editorial assessment of the losses occurs on p. 120.
Announcement, 5 February 2016, paragraphs on the basins at Agua Clara and Cocolí and reuse of water from Gatún Lake per lockage.
23 March 2016. Paragraphs describing two training lakes, a reproduction of Culebra Cut, the 1:25 models used by pilots and tug captains, the Maersk Edinburgh model, and wave and wind generators.

20 June 2016, first two paragraphs. Identifies the successful Pacific-side trial by the US-built crane ship Oceanus and names pilots Fernando Jaén and Ricardo Varela. The commercial inauguration was still six days away.

1 January 2020. Opening announcement and biographical section “About Mrs. Ilya Espino de Marotta”. The only woman engineer at the shipyard in 1985; resources management and project controls; engineering leadership of the expansion; first woman deputy administrator.

29 April 2016, paragraphs identifying the two participating lines and their ships Andronikos and Thalatta, the venue, the notary, Jorge Quijano, the drawing of the two names and the selected ship’s length and beam.

30 April 2016. Opening paragraphs describe the previous morning’s draw in the rotunda using the national lottery urn. Reporter names Margarita Azucena, notary Víctor Aldana Aparicio and administrator Jorge Quijano, and identifies both ships.

Morning dispatch, 26 June 2016. Opening paragraphs identify the vessel formerly named Andronikos, departure from Piraeus and the start at Agua Clara; the Pacific-side passage was still expected as this was written.

Final communiqué, 26 June 2016, paragraph beginning “The inaugural transit began”. Records a completed passage from Agua Clara on the Atlantic to Cocolí on the Pacific by Cosco Shipping Panama, bound for Asia.

Spanish section, pp. 29–30, “Crónica de un día inolvidable”, arrivals by bus, crowd at noon, entry at about 3 p.m. and ship’s horn at Cocolí. P. 53, training and chartered Baroque. English section, p. 191, completed inauguration and more than 200 transits through September; p. 193, Baroque and Oceanus trials.
Opening paragraphs on the 7 January 1914 completion of a staged crossing by the old French crane boat Alexandre La Valley and the inauguration with John A. Constantine serving as pilot aboard Ancon.

Chairman’s message, opening paragraph on 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024. Printed p. 22, Water Use, graph 1, 542 hm³ for drinking water, 17% of 3,124 hm³; p. 23, Rainfall, graph 2, watershed rainfall of 2,118 mm and historical average 2,660 mm; p. 24, Pilot Plan for Water Treatment, April 2024 reverse-osmosis pilot at Escobal for a projected 2,500 residents.

1 May 2024, opening four paragraphs, fig. 1 and Main findings. May–December 2023 rainfall near the Gatún catchment, lake levels, ship number and size restrictions, rising urban demand and leakage, influence of El Niño, differing station trends and insufficient evidence for attribution of observed drying to human-caused warming.

20 October 2023. Image description, on Sentinel-1 radar observations and year-colour assignment, and the Credits and Licence fields for the 1,623 × 1,623 JPEG. Blue 2020, green 2021, red 2022, with ships on Gatún Lake and offshore. CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO is an explicit licence option.

PDF p. 1, paragraph giving the lake reference point 09°10′31.7″ N, 79°54′06.4″ W, with cross-references to the national mapping institute. PDF pp. 3–5, fishery and tables 1–2, listing Escobal among the fishing communities. The fisheries figures cited there come from 2004.
GeoNames 3703443, Panama City, national capital. Coordinates 8.99360, −79.51973. The capital represents the nationwide referendum.
“Centro de Visitantes de Agua Clara – Gatún” and “Exhibición panorámica”. The public visitor site overlooks the Caribbean-side works near Colón.
Map entry for the public visitor centre, OpenStreetMap node 4593152300, 9.26486, −79.90954, with the Agua Clara Locks to the northwest. Rounded regional map reference.
GeoNames 3712135, populated place Cocolí, 8.98449, −79.59775. Rounded locality point for the Pacific-side trial.

labels.de: Wie viel Wasser braucht der erweiterte Panamakanal?
labels.en: How much water does the expanded Panama Canal need?

labels.de: 22. Oktober 2006 · Panama stimmt über größere Schleusen ab
labels.en: 22 October 2006 · Panama votes on wider locks

summary.de: Landesweit stimmen 705.284 Menschen für und 201.105 gegen den Ausbau. Regierung und Parlament hatten bereits zugestimmt. Der Kartenpunkt in der Hauptstadt steht für das landesweite Votum.
summary.en: Voters across Panama cast 705,284 yes votes and 201,105 no votes after the government and legislature approved the expansion. The capital represents the nationwide vote.

labels.de: 5. Februar 2016, Meldung der Kanalbehörde · Das erste Sparbecken in Agua Clara wird erprobt
labels.en: 5 February 2016, authority announcement · Testing starts at the first basin in Agua Clara

summary.de: Die Kanalbehörde meldet den Beginn der Tests an einem Becken der obersten Kammer. Seitliche Becken speichern Wasser für eine weitere Schleusung. Als Ortsbezug dient das Besucherzentrum bei Colón.
summary.en: The canal authority reports testing at a basin beside the upper chamber. The basins hold water for another lockage. The visitor centre near Colón marks the area.

labels.de: 20. Juni 2016 · Zwei Lotsen steuern die Oceanus durch Cocolí
labels.en: 20 June 2016 · Two pilots take Oceanus through Cocolí

summary.de: Fernando Jaén und Ricardo Varela steuern ein Kranschiff durch die neuen Pazifikschleusen. Die technische Leitung des Ausbauprogramms hat Ilya Espino de Marotta. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Ort Cocolí.
summary.en: Fernando Jaén and Ricardo Varela take a crane ship through the new Pacific locks. Ilya Espino de Marotta led engineering for the expansion. The point marks the locality of Cocolí.

labels.de: 26. Juni 2016 · Die Cosco Shipping Panama fährt von Meer zu Meer
labels.en: 26 June 2016 · Cosco Shipping Panama crosses from sea to sea

summary.de: Die erste kommerzielle Durchfahrt beginnt in Agua Clara am Atlantik und endet in Cocolí am Pazifik. Die Karte markiert die Karibikseite beim heutigen Besucherzentrum.
summary.en: The inaugural commercial passage starts at Agua Clara on the Atlantic and ends at Cocolí on the Pacific. The map marks the Caribbean side at today’s visitor centre.

labels.de: 1. Oktober 2023 bis 30. September 2024 · Wenig Regen im Einzugsgebiet des Kanals
labels.en: 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024 · A rain shortage in the canal watershed

summary.de: Für das Geschäftsjahr 2023/24 verzeichnet die Kanalbehörde 2.118 Millimeter Regen im Einzugsgebiet und 542 Millionen Kubikmeter für Trinkwasser. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Gatúnsee. Die ESA-Aufnahmen stammen aus den Jahren vor der trockenen Regenzeit.
summary.en: For fiscal year 2023/24 the authority records 2,118 millimetres of rain across the watershed and 542 million cubic metres for drinking water. The point represents Gatún Lake. The ESA imagery predates the dry rainy season.

summary.de: Panama stimmt über größere Schleusen ab. Zwei Lotsen erproben sie auf einem Kranschiff, bevor ein ausgelostes Containerschiff die Meere wechselt. Als Jahre später ungewöhnlich wenig Regen fällt, brauchen Schiffe und Ufergemeinden das Wasser desselben Sees.
summary.en: Panamanians vote on wider locks. Two pilots take a crane ship through on trial, and a container ship wins the right to cross first. When the rains fall short years later, the ships and the communities on the shore need water from the same lake.

sourceRefs.locator: New West Indian Guide 59 (1–2), pp. 1–26. On pp. 8–10 Richardson cites Karner's letter in the Barbados Advocate, 23 January 1905, and the 1909 Weekly Illustrated Paper retrospective on recruitment by returnees. Bridgetown wharf, lighters, Carlisle Bay and the distinction between contracted and noncontract migrants appear on pp. 9–10.

Workforce recruitment, from the paragraph beginning ‘It was recognized early on’ through the separate discussions of Barbados and Jamaica. The figure of 19,900 is recruitment in Barbados. Jamaica refused recruiting and required intending emigrants to cover tax and passage. Skilled workers were among those able to pay.

Property 1376, Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison, N 13°05′48″ W 59°36′50″ and the accompanying property map. Locator for the historic town and its harbour rather than an individual 1905 boarding place.

Prologue 29 (2). Notes 1 and 2 identify Commissary manager to J. F. Stevens, 15 February 1907, and Stevens to W. C. Gorgas, 30 November 1906, both RG 185, General Correspondence 1904–14, file 2-C-55, part 1. Quotations, financial bonds, equivalent silver pay and access to facilities appear in the opening discussion of the two rolls.

Proceedings reporting Stevens's correspondence of 9 and 30 November 1906. The separate letter concerning the joint telephone and telegraph line is explicitly dated ‘Culebra, Canal Zone, November 30, 1906’ and places his office on the day of the payroll letter. The content of the payroll instruction is in RG 185, file 2-C-55.

Annex 4, Figure 1, between printed pp. 2 and 3. Overlay of the 1909 street plan labelled ‘Old town of Culebra’ on the March 1947 contours and slide limits. Approximate site on the west bank near Zion Hill. Neither the pay-car siding nor the precise 1906 office is identified on this map.

National Archives Identifier 100997804, caption 311-A on the photograph. The dated print shows staff and workers at the pay car. The NARA/DPLA item record and US public-domain statement accompany the 1,761 × 1,443 pixel file.

Scribner’s Magazine 57 (4), April 1915, p. 396 (wage rolls and European labourers) and p. 404, photograph caption ‘Pay car at Culebra, January 12, 1908’: the carriage had counters and separate entrance and exit. This is an account by the former chief engineer and then governor.

AA00016037/00101, typescript pp. 1–3 (scan files image0029–image0031). Arrival by railway at San Pablo in 1908, coal and track work, father's referral, friends at Tabernilla, January 1910 move to the Gatún spillway, railway assignments and the concrete crane. The date and location of his first shift follow the first-person text.

Interview and transcript, 17 July 2020, AA00081353/00001. At 07:27–08:46 Moore recalls her birthplace and date, at 14:52–18:00 her father's farriery in Barbados and blacksmithing in the Balboa shops and her older sister, at 23:10 the shared facilities, at 39:38 the commissary books, at 57:45–58:18 her work and at 59:04–1:00:24 Manuel's Chinese shop and credit.

Modern American History 7 (1), pp. 131–135. Opening pages, especially note 3 on the Moore oral history and the 1920 and 1930 censuses, notes 8–10 on food, domestic work and remittances, figure 1 and note 11 on Adica Moore's work. The 22 January 1965 Spillway photograph documents her later career.
La Boca neighbourhood record, Location, 8.94811° N, 79.5613° W. Modern neighbourhood locator at the Pacific entrance. No individual family's house, shop or 1910 workplace is claimed.

Biblioteca Nacional de Panamá, ‘Martes 24 de febrero de 1920’, printed pp. 341–344: strike call, itemised demands, Governor Harding's refusal to conclude an agreement with a committee. The dated chronology distinguishes the strike call and walkout from preparatory activity.

Governor's report, pp. 26–27, increases in living costs, demand for seven cents per hour, participation estimate and terms of re-employment. Chief Quartermaster's report, ‘Strike of silver employees’, pp. 135–136, commissary disruptions and volunteer replacements.

Paragraph beginning ‘El gobernador de la Zona del Canal de Panamá’, on the 24 February walkout and strong participation in Colón. Accounts differ on the overall number, for which the chapter explicitly attributes its range to the governor’s report.
TGN 7006458, coordinates 9.3500 N, 79.9000 W, Aspinwall as alternative name, historical note on the northern terminus. City-level point on Manzanillo Island.

AA00016037/00033, typescript pp. 1–3, scans image0096–image0098. Page 1 gives his Colón address and Panamanian citizenship, recalls Bajo Matachín, names Marian Cunningson and Caroline Lowe and prices their breakfast. Page 2 records 18 years as an artisan and 30 on deck, and his tally of 5,330 transits.

AA00016037/00001, scans image0003–image0004, ‘The Contest’ and ‘The Entries’, for the circular sent to fifteen newspapers, relief packages, posting deadline and anniversary. List of entrants on image0005 and image0007 includes Clarke and Simmons.

Modern American History 7 (1), pp. 127–130, especially pp. 127 and 130. The author identifies the 112 written testimonies in Box 25 of the Isthmian Historical Society collection at the Library of Congress and discusses how they were solicited and kept.

labels.en: The people who worked on the Panama Canal

labels.de: 23. Januar 1905 · Wer in Bridgetown an Bord ging

summary.de: William J. Karner wirbt im Barbados Advocate um Arbeitskräfte für die Kanalbaukommission. Später erzählen Rückkehrer in den Dörfern von ihren Erfahrungen, und am Kai von Bridgetown verabschieden Familien die nächsten Reisenden.
summary.en: William J. Karner appeals for canal recruits in the Barbados Advocate. Men returning to the island share their experiences, and families gather at the Bridgetown wharf to see off those who follow.

labels.de: 30. November 1906 · Ein Brief entscheidet über die Lohnliste
labels.en: 30 November 1906 · A letter about the payroll

summary.de: John F. Stevens weist William Gorgas an, Schwarze Beschäftigte unter bestimmten Bedingungen auf die Silberliste zu setzen. Im Schriftwechsel über diese Einteilung kommen auch die Schwarzen Abteilungsleiter und Verkäufer der Verwaltungsläden zu Wort, allerdings nur durch ihren Vorgesetzten.
summary.en: John F. Stevens instructs William Gorgas to transfer Black employees to the silver roll under specified conditions. Further correspondence records Black department heads and sales staff in the commissaries through the voice of their manager.

labels.de: 12. Januar 1908 · Der Lohnwagen und der erste Arbeitstag
labels.en: 12 January 1908 · The pay car and the first day's work

summary.de: Ein Foto zeigt Männer am Zahlwagen in Culebra. Wie unterschiedlich ihre Berufswege sein konnten, erzählt Edgar Llewellyn Simmons, der 1908 Kohle schaufelte und später in Gatún als Bremser und Weichensteller arbeitete.
summary.en: A photograph shows workers at the Culebra pay car. Edgar Llewellyn Simmons recalled unloading coal in 1908 and later working as a brakeman and switch tender in Gatún.

labels.en: 1910 · Making a home in La Boca

summary.de: Emily Amelia Lewis reist zu William Edward Griffith nach Panama. Die Erinnerungen ihrer Tochter Adica Moore führen aus der gemeinsamen Wohnung in La Boca in Manuels Lebensmittelladen und an ihren späteren Arbeitsplatz im Krankenhaus.
summary.en: Emily Amelia Lewis joins William Edward Griffith in Panama. Their daughter Adica Moore's recollections lead from the family home in La Boca to Manuel's grocery shop and her own later workplace at the hospital.

labels.de: 24. Februar 1920 · Am 24. Februar bleibt die Arbeit liegen

summary.de: Beschäftigte der Silberliste legen die Arbeit nieder. Colón ist eines der Zentren. Der Gouverneur schätzt die Beteiligung an der gesamten Aktion auf 15.000 bis 17.000 Beschäftigte.
summary.en: Silver employees go on strike, with strong support in Colón. The governor estimates 15,000 to 17,000 people joined the walkout across the canal workforce.

labels.en: 1963 · What Clarke wrote down in Colón

summary.de: In seiner Einsendung für den Wettbewerb von 1963 erinnert sich Amos E. Clarke aus Colón an Marian Cunningson und Caroline Lowe, die Jahre zuvor Arbeiter in Bajo Matachín mit Frühstück versorgten.
summary.en: Writing from Colón for the 1963 competition, Amos E. Clarke recalls Marian Cunningson and Caroline Lowe, who sold breakfast to canal workers many years earlier at Bajo Matachín.

summary.de: Ein Frühstück an der Baustelle, ein Lohnwagen in Culebra und vier Familien mit einem Waschplatz in La Boca. Arbeiterinnen und Arbeiter erzählen, was es kostete, am Kanal zu leben, und welche Ansprüche sie durchzusetzen versuchten.
summary.en: Breakfast at a worksite, a pay car at Culebra and four families sharing a washroom at La Boca. Canal workers recall what it took to make a living and the rights they fought to secure.

sourceRefs.locator: The Canal Record, vol. V, no. 15, 6 December 1911, pp. 120–121. First column on the expected removal of the railway and dwellings already being taken down. The entries for Gatun, Bohio and Frijoles list the produce trade, housing, school and shops, 1908 counts and the burial of old Gatun under the dam. The editorial assessment of the losses occurs on p. 120.

La Prensa, 6 July 2014. The paragraphs beginning “A diferencia de lo que se cree comúnmente” and “Además, los trabajos del Canal” distinguish flooded Gorgona, the first relocation of Gatún and the later clearance of dry settlements. The preceding paragraphs reconstruct commerce and housing from tax records.

Volume 50, pp. 2534–2535, “Relocation of Panama Railroad.” The engineering account reproduced here distinguishes the closure at Gatun on 9 February and the new Gatun–Matachin service on 15 February 1912. It describes the progression of flooding on the old right of way.

Cuadernos Nacionales 37, pp. 151–154, section “Estación de Gatún.” Figures 32 and 36 locate the original and relocated railway station and relate the latter to the buildings and shoreline. Figure 33 and the text on pp. 152–153 describe the platform, ticket office, telegraph and baggage room.

La Estrella de Panamá, 11 November 2023. Caption to the plan of finca 1723 and section “Los nuevos poblados” on the 200-hectare purchase in July 1913, residents from different settlements, and journeys to the outskirts of Panama City. For the storage site and the speech the accompanying chapter uses the contemporary English-language report.

The Canal Record, vol. VII, no. 19, 31 December 1913, p. 174. Account of the 30 December dedication, the bishop’s tablet, Tomás Posada’s address for the residents, building materials on dump No. 6, water, agricultural land and the bridge. The closing paragraph gives the population estimate and distinguishes temporary from rebuilt houses.

In Ashley Carse et al., Panama Canal Forum, Environmental History 21(2), pp. 240–249. See pp. 241–242 on the dry site of New Gatún and its 1914 clearance, pp. 246–247 on Chagres, and p. 249, notes 26–30, on the 8 December 1915 request, Panama’s reply, the residents’ acta dated 31 January 1916 and the moving-cost correspondence.

The Canal Record, vol. VIII. Joint Land Commission, docket 1884, opinion of 26 October 1914. Reproduces the executive order signed 5 December 1912 and the 5 June 1914 cancellation notice for Lot 8, Block 5, village of Empire. The final paragraphs establish the commission’s jurisdiction over this leasehold claim.

Chronology of Smithsonian History, record 230, 17 April 1923. The entry names Governor Jay J. Morrow, identifies the creation of the island by flooding and distinguishes the reserve declaration from the construction of the laboratory.

Smithsonian Miscellaneous Collections 78(8), pp. 1–2. Standley describes the laboratory window, the submerged town of Bohío, dead tree trunks in the inlets, abandoned fields with secondary vegetation and his observations of wooded ravines.

Introduction, first paragraphs on the flooding of the lower Chagres valley, old growth, secondary growth and small farms, and the purchase of the remaining smallholders’ interests when the island became a reserve.
Gazetteer ID 3709287, dam in Colón, 9.262778° N, 79.930000° W. Rounded to 9.26° N, 79.93° W to identify the dam area covering the old village; the 1911 account supplies the historical association.
Gazetteer ID 3703839 for the settlement in Chame, Panamá Oeste, 8.554786° N, 79.874269° W. Rounded point for the coastal settlement founded in 1913.

Component 1582rev-001, Castle of San Lorenzo. Coordinates 9°19′23.42″ N, 79°59′59.19″ W are rounded for orientation at the old port near the fort, as located by Lasso. The mapped marker indicates the river mouth.
Section 2.1 and island outline. The survey gives bounds of 9°08′–9°11′ N and 79°49′–79°52′ W. The marker is an approximate point within the island.

Stereograph Cards collection, Library of Congress control number 2002697845, digital identifier LC-DIG-stereo-1s34806. Color halftone print on a stereograph card made in the United States, catalogued about 1900. The caption names old Gorgona. Rights advisory: no known restrictions on publication.

Memorias 58, pp. 23–25. Panamanian foreign ministry, 1916, pp. 331–332, records the 31 January inspection and the selection by local officials and residents of the site opposite the village of Lagarto. The Canal Record, 14 June 1916, p. 365, reports the first trip with residents, household goods and animals. Descendants recall that some families settled elsewhere. DOI 10.14482/memor.58.121.526.

labels.de: Der Gatúnsee und die Orte, die umziehen mussten
labels.en: Gatun Lake and the towns that had to move

labels.de: 1908 · Gatún räumt den Platz für den Damm
labels.en: 1908 · Gatún moves from the dam site

summary.de: Das Dorf am Fluss ist 1908 aufgegeben. Die meisten Gebäude stehen danach wieder in Nuevo Gatún. Fels und Erde des Damms bedecken den früheren Standort.
summary.en: The riverside village has been abandoned by 1908. Most of its buildings are re-erected at Nuevo Gatún. Earth and rock for the dam cover the old site.

labels.de: 15. Februar 1912 · Die Bahn eröffnet die Strecke Gatún–Matachín
labels.en: 15 February 1912 · The relocated Gatún–Matachín line opens

summary.de: Die Züge nehmen die neue Strecke. Das Wasser erreicht nach und nach das Gleisbett der alten Bahn. Einige Haushalte hatten ihre Häuser schon vor der Flutung zerlegt.
summary.en: Rail traffic shifts to the new line. Water progressively covers the old right of way. Some households had already dismantled their homes before the flood.

labels.de: 30. Dezember 1913 · Tomás Posada spricht bei der Einweihung von Nueva Gorgona
labels.en: 30 December 1913 · Tomás Posada speaks at the dedication of Nueva Gorgona

summary.de: Beim Fest an der Pazifikküste fordert ein Einwohner Wasser, Ackerland, eine Brücke über den Chame und das Baumaterial der alten Häuser. Das frühere Gorgona am Chagres wird überflutet.
summary.en: At the Pacific dedication a resident asks for water, farmland, a bridge across the Chame and the material from people’s old houses. The original Gorgona on the Chagres is flooded.

labels.de: 8. Dezember 1915 · Goethals verlangt das Land an der Chagresmündung
labels.en: 8 December 1915 · Goethals requests the land at the mouth of the Chagres

summary.de: Goethals verlangt von Präsident Porras den alten Hafen. Der Bürgermeister und weitere Einwohner wählen im Januar 1916 einen neuen Standort an der Mündung des Río Lagarto. Im Juni beginnt der Umzug.
summary.en: Goethals asks President Porras for the old port. In January 1916 the mayor and other residents select a new site at the mouth of the Lagarto River. The move begins in June.

labels.de: 17. April 1923 · Barro Colorado wird zum Schutzgebiet erklärt
labels.en: 17 April 1923 · Barro Colorado is declared a reserve

summary.de: Gouverneur Jay J. Morrow weist die durch den Stausee entstandene Insel als Schutzgebiet aus. Im späteren Wald findet der Botaniker Paul Standley noch die Spuren früherer Felder.
summary.en: Governor Jay J. Morrow sets aside the island formed by impounding the Chagres. Botanist Paul Standley later records evidence of farm clearings in its forest.

summary.de: Unter dem Damm liegt Alt-Gatún. An der Pazifikküste wartet Nueva Gorgona auf Baumaterial. Eine Rede bei der Ortseinweihung, eine Eingabe am Chagres und ein botanischer Bericht erzählen von den Menschen an den Ufern des neuen Sees.
summary.en: Old Gatún lies under the dam. On the Pacific coast, Nueva Gorgona awaits the pieces of dismantled houses. A resident’s speech, a petition at the mouth of the Chagres and a botanical survey reveal who lived along the new lake’s shores.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 November 2021, “Antecedentes históricos” and “Antes de la segunda guerra mundial”: September 1882 opening, choice of the slope of Cerro Ancón to catch breezes away from city wastewater, US acquisition and reuse of the grounds. MINSA gives 12 September for the opening. The thanksgiving Mass is separately dated to the 17th by Escobar. The station therefore identifies the opening by month.

Chapter VI, “Hospitales en la Época del Canal Francés”, pp. CXLIX–CLI. Companyo, his earlier work at Suez, Huerta de Gallo, the fundraising committee, the September thanksgiving Mass, transfers of patients, the sisters, Colón, the former Taboga hotel and the orphanage. Chapter VII, pp. CLXXIV–CLXXVI, reports the 1916 request for larger premises and lottery funding. Pp. CLXXXII–CLXXXIII name the four nursing graduates of 1912. For the 1924 opening date use the contemporary decrees, which supersede the December date printed on p. CLXXV.

“Gustave Eiffel”, final paragraphs on the first canal company, receivership and the appointment of a liquidator. Escobar, pp. CL–CLI, traces how the breakdown of the construction enterprise affected its hospitals.

Public Health Reports 19 (8), 19 February 1904, printed p. 277, “Hospitals”: wooden, separated pavilions of the French hospital, nursing by Sisters of Charity, twenty-four patients in the foreign section and twenty in the canal section. This is a count made before the US canal administration assumed the hospital.

Minutes, 118th meeting at Washington, 24 December 1906, printed p. 49, item 2. The Chief Sanitary Officer’s 1 December communication gives 7 June 1904 as the beginning of the service of “Miss M. Eugenie Hibbard” as chief nurse at Ancon Hospital. This is the credited start of her appointment.

The Panama Canal Review en Español, spring 1976, printed pp. 32–33. Hernández calls her Mary Eugene Hibbard, dates her appointment to June 1904, describes her arrival with Gorgas and two nurses, and quotes her recollections of some 75 scattered buildings and the five buildings selected for ward and service uses.

Doctoral thesis, printed p. 50, citing Rodríguez on the 1904 appointment and 1908 count of 117 nurses among 205 US women employed in the Canal Zone. Note 49 quotes La Estrella de Panamá, 9 February 1905, vol. LVI, no. 13544, p. 10, on malaria admissions and the latrines at Ancón. Pp. 52–53 quote the same newspaper of 13 March 1909 on admission of single women aged sixteen to twenty-five at Santo Tomás.

Service Records Cards, 1904–1920, series NAID 7226556. Illustration captioned “Miss Anna L. Doolittle, June 21, 1907 Service Card”, recto and verso, followed by Brown’s identification of her age, home in West Virginia and Ancon Hospital appointment. The full-size image linked farther down is separately identified as Ward 9, NAID 6120319.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 719, pp. 707–708. Enclosure is dated 20 January, cover letter 24 January, supplementary note 25 January. Eighteen official reports since 1 July 1904 included the four sanitary labourers still in hospital on 20 January. Three deaths, the cities and intervening zone, bills of health for shipping and the reported recoveries appear in the circular and note.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 718, pp. 706–707, especially enclosure 2, the translated reply of Panama’s minister of government and foreign affairs, 21 January 1905. De la Guardia explains his authorization and the changes suggested by his office when accepting the sanitary regulations under article VII.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 723, enclosure 2, paragraph beginning “Immediately after seeing”. Barrett locates the legation near the corner of the canal building and the Plaza. The square serves only to orient the January circular in the capital. Its text gives no legation street address.

Societas 19 (1), 73–91, printed p. 78. Paragraph immediately preceding “El puerto de La Boca – Balboa”: engineers’ selection of the old French reservoir on the upper Río Grande and water running through Panama City’s mains on 4 July 1905.

Passages following the reorganization under David H. Brandon. The hydrant system was inaugurated in Cathedral Square on 4 July 1905. At the Malambo fire of 12 January 1906 the firefighters used pumps connected to cisterns.

Printed pp. 178–179, paragraph beginning “Uno de tales proyectos”: the Star and Herald / La Estrella called for water mains in the 1880s for drinking water and fire protection and reported on the municipal water contract in 1888.

Environmental History 21 (2), 250–259. Final paragraphs before “Panamanian Resistance” and paragraphs 1–4 of that section, notes 11–15. Describes rainwater, water peddlers, cisterns and ceramic tinajas, the reach of the dipper, topping up jars, complaints when inspectors emptied them and reports of residents concealing their jars.

National Archives Identifier 6120319, 185-G-16-1514, August 1919. National Archives Foundation, DocsTeach, “Citation” and item-specific “Rights: Public Domain”. The photographer is unnamed. The lower edge of the surviving print reads 284-X8, whereas the DocsTeach transcription renders 248-X8. Both identify the same image by title, month and NAID.

Image 88b710, source “The U.S. National Archives”, copyright field “No known copyright restrictions”. The photographic caption dates the picture to August 1919, without a day. The matched, full-size scan of NAID 6120319 used here is the one provided by the Archives on its Rediscovering Black History page.

The Panama Canal Record, vol. XIII, no. 1, 20 August 1919, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 26), table for the new hospital buildings. Section C, ward 9: 39 beds, official category “White foreign, male”. Wards 10–14 are separately classified. Compare visiting hours in sections A and C, and the note below the table assigning emergency passes to the section nurse.

Prologue 29 (2). Notes 1 and 2 identify Commissary manager to J. F. Stevens, 15 February 1907, and Stevens to W. C. Gorgas, 30 November 1906, both RG 185, General Correspondence 1904–14, file 2-C-55, part 1. Quotations, financial bonds, equivalent silver pay and access to facilities appear in the opening discussion of the two rolls.

Decree of 2 September 1924, Gaceta Oficial no. 4487, 13 September 1924, printed p. 393, left column, “Artículo único”, signed Porras and Jiménez. Decree of 7 March 1924, arts. 1 and 3. The former exhibition grounds and the intended opening on 1 September are explicit. The programme is to include a reception and celebrations for administrative staff and convalescent patients. These are instructions for the celebration.

Memoria del Hospital Santo Tomás 2020–2021, “Recordar es vivir”, caption and opening paragraph. The institution identifies the ceremony and the inauguration by President Belisario Porras on 1 September 1924.

Chapter XVI, “Malaria Work and the Hospital System”, printed p. 226, paragraph beginning “The nursing force was composed”. Gorgas describes the Black maids and orderlies who worked in the French hospital, including direct care and manual work under the sisters’ supervision.

1 May 2024, opening four paragraphs, fig. 1 and Main findings. May–December 2023 rainfall near the Gatún catchment, lake levels, ship number and size restrictions, rising urban demand and leakage, influence of El Niño, differing station trends and insufficient evidence for attribution of observed drying to human-caused warming.

labels.de: Wer in Panama die Kranken pflegte
labels.en: Caring for the sick on the Panama isthmus

labels.de: September 1882 · Die Schwestern am Cerro Ancón
labels.en: September 1882 · The sisters on Ancón Hill

summary.de: Die französische Kanalgesellschaft eröffnete auf dem Hang ihr Zentralkrankenhaus. Die Schwestern vom heiligen Vinzenz von Paul empfingen dort auch Kranke aus den Stationen entlang der Kanalbaustellen.
summary.en: The French canal company opened its central hospital on the hill. The Sisters of St Vincent de Paul received patients referred by dispensaries along the excavations.

labels.de: 7. Juni 1904 · Hibbard übernimmt die Leitung der Krankenpflege
labels.en: 7 June 1904 · Hibbard takes charge of nursing

summary.de: Die Kommission rechnete Hibbards Dienstzeit vom 7. Juni an. In Ancón suchte sie fünf Gebäude für die Patienten und die Versorgung der Stationen aus.
summary.en: The commission credited Hibbard’s service from 7 June. At Ancón she chose five buildings to house the patients and the services the wards needed.

labels.de: 20. Januar 1905 · Barrett meldet vier Patienten im Krankenhaus
labels.en: 20 January 1905 · Barrett reports four patients in hospital

summary.de: John Barrett meldete am 20. Januar, vier Arbeiter des Sanitätsdienstes würden noch wegen Gelbfiebers behandelt. Sie gehörten zu den 18 seit Juli 1904 gemeldeten Fällen. Der Platz dient zur Orientierung in der Nähe der Gesandtschaft.
summary.en: John Barrett reported on 20 January that four sanitary labourers were still in hospital with yellow fever. They were among the eighteen cases reported since July 1904. The square marks the vicinity of the legation.

summary.de: In Panama-Stadt floss Wasser aus dem oberen Río Grande durch die neuen Leitungen. Die Feuerwehr überliefert die Einweihung der Hydranten auf dem Kathedralplatz und einen späteren Brand, bei dem sie noch Zisternen nutzte.
summary.en: Water from the upper Río Grande entered Panama City’s new mains. The fire brigade records the opening of the hydrant system in Cathedral Square and a subsequent fire at which it still used cisterns.

labels.en: August 1919 · Visiting hours in Ward Nine

summary.de: Im Aufnahmevermerk steht „Spanish“. Der Besuchsplan nennt 39 Betten für Männer, die als weiß und ausländisch eingestuft wurden. Die Angehörigen hatten in diesem Teil des Krankenhauses anderthalb Stunden Besuchszeit.
summary.en: The print labels the ward “Spanish”. The visiting schedule lists thirty-nine beds for men classified as white and foreign. Families had a ninety-minute visiting period on the designated days in this part of the hospital.

labels.de: 1. September 1924 · Einweihung des Hospital Santo Tomás in Calidonia
labels.en: 1 September 1924 · Hospital Santo Tomás opens in Calidonia

summary.de: Präsident Porras eröffnete den Neubau des panamaischen Krankenhauses auf dem früheren Ausstellungsgelände. Sein Dekret vom 2. September erklärte das von der Nation errichtete Haus für den öffentlichen Dienst eröffnet.
summary.en: President Porras inaugurated the Panamanian hospital’s new buildings on the former exhibition grounds. His decree of 2 September declared the hospital built by the nation open for public service.

summary.de: Ordensschwestern, Pflegerinnen und Angehörige sorgten für die Kranken am Panamakanal. Ein Wasserkrug, eine Gelbfiebermeldung und der Besuchsplan von Ancón erzählen, was das für Familien in Panama bedeutete.
summary.en: Sisters, nurses and relatives cared for the sick on the isthmus. A household water jar, a yellow fever circular and the visiting hours at Ancón show what that meant for families in Panama.

description.de: 1801–1900. Ein kalendarischer Zeitbereich; regionale Epochen können ihn unterschiedlich gliedern.
description.en: 1801–1900. A calendar grouping; regional periods may divide it differently.

sourceRefs.locator: Paragraphs on lock steps and origin of construction cement, gravity and locomotives. Concluding paragraphs cover shovels 222 and 230 on 20 May 1913, locomotive 260 on 10 September, the Gatun tug on 26 September and Marmot’s December cut at Cucaracha.

Paragraphs on rail transport of spoil to Gatún Dam and the Naos–Flamenco breakwater, on extending the lake across the divide, and on the distinct modes of slope movement in the Culebra and Cucaracha slides.

Report of Electrical and Mechanical Engineer, pp. 115–116, “Up lockage of tug Gatun” and its return. Measured lift 64.7 feet. Pp. 118–119, first passage of the west chamber at Pedro Miguel by La Valley with Clapet No. 9 and barge No. 6, and trial at Gatún by the Ancon on 11 June.

Description of the canal, pp. 46–48, Gatun Lake, Gaillard Cut, Miraflores Lake and Locks. The bottom was 40 ft above sea level and the lake provided a channel 45 ft deep. P. 48 describes the paired chambers, three flights and the effect of Pacific tides on the lift at Miraflores.
Opening paragraphs on the 7 January 1914 completion of a staged crossing by the old French crane boat Alexandre La Valley and the inauguration with John A. Constantine serving as pilot aboard Ancon.

Tenth year, no. 2948, 16 August 1914, p. 1, col. 3 (digital file, pp. 2–3). Account of the special train and sailing from Cristóbal, lunch and steward Leddeke, Gamboa and dredge crews, spectators at Pedro Miguel, the outer buoys, transfer to boats and the anthem for President Porras.

Vol. VIII, no. 6, p. 52, letter dated 24 September 1914, opening paragraphs. The report distinguishes the 3 August Cristobal test to Balboa from the 15 August Ancon deep-water passage, then counts six vessels on 16 August.

The New Encyclopedic Atlas and Gazetteer of the World (1914), p. 66. Map of the route through Gatún Lake and the cut to the Pacific locks, with the railway, grid index, settlement names and coastal approaches.

Record Group 185, local identifier 185-G-0888, NAID 100996356. View from Cerro Luisa, 15 August 1914. Cropped archival photograph, file page with creator, identified location, date and public-domain status.

Governor’s report, discussion of Gaillard Cut slides and general reopening on 15 April 1916. Appendix E, plates 45, 48, 50, 54 and 56, shows the September working face and subsequent obstruction. “Lockages”, p. 76, records about forty southbound vessels returning through Gatún.
Announcement, 5 February 2016, paragraphs on the basins at Agua Clara and Cocolí and reuse of water from Gatún Lake per lockage.
GeoNames 3709435, section of canal, 9.05597, −79.65663. The point represents the cut as a whole. It does not locate a particular shovel, train or slide face.

labels.de: Mit der Ancon über die Wasserscheide
labels.en: Across the continental divide aboard Ancon

labels.de: 10. September 1913 · Der letzte Zug mit trocken gebaggertem Gestein
labels.en: 10 September 1913 · The last trainload of rock dug out on dry ground

summary.de: Lokomotive 260 zog die letzte auf trockenem Grund gebaggerte Fuhre aus dem Culebra-Einschnitt. Nach der Flutung gewannen Schwimmbagger die Fahrrinne zurück. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Einschnitt.
summary.en: Locomotive 260 hauled the last rock dug on dry ground from Culebra Cut. After flooding, floating dredges cleared the channel. The point identifies the cut.

labels.de: 26. September 1913 · Der Schlepper Gatun fährt durch drei Stufen
labels.en: 26 September 1913 · The tug Gatun ascends three steps

summary.de: Der Schlepper stieg bei der ersten Probeschleusung knapp zwanzig Meter. Am nächsten Morgen kehrte er durch dieselben Kammern zur Atlantikseite zurück.
summary.en: The working tug climbed nearly twenty metres in the first trial through the locks. Next morning it came down through the same flight to the Atlantic side.

labels.de: 7. Januar 1914 · Ein Kranschiff erreicht den Pazifik
labels.en: 7 January 1914 · A crane boat reaches the Pacific

summary.de: Die französische Alexandre La Valley, zuvor von der Atlantikseite heraufgekommen, fuhr durch die Pazifikschleusen. Damit hatte das Arbeitsschiff die Landenge in Etappen durchquert.
summary.en: The French crane boat Alexandre La Valley, previously brought up from the Atlantic side, passed through the Pacific locks, completing a crossing in stages.

labels.de: 15. August 1914 · Die Ancon auf der offiziellen Eröffnungsfahrt
labels.en: 15 August 1914 · Ancon on the official opening passage

summary.de: Der Lotse John A. Constantine führte den Dampfer von Cristóbal bis zu den äußeren pazifischen Fahrwassertonnen. Eine Aufnahme vom Cerro Luisa zeigt das Einlaufen in Pedro Miguel.
summary.en: The pilot John A. Constantine took the steamer from Cristóbal to the outer Pacific buoys. A photograph from Cerro Luisa shows it entering Pedro Miguel Locks.

labels.de: 18. September 1915 bis 15. April 1916 · Die Hänge schließen die Fahrrinne
labels.en: 18 September 1915 to 15 April 1916 · The banks close over the channel

summary.de: Die Hänge von Culebra schoben Material von beiden Seiten in die Fahrrinne. Rund vierzig Schiffe mussten über Gatún zum Atlantik zurück. Im April 1916 begann der reguläre Verkehr erneut.
summary.en: Moving slopes at Culebra sent material into the channel from both sides. Roughly forty vessels had to return through Gatún to the Atlantic. General traffic resumed in April 1916.

summary.de: Ein Schlepper steigt zum noch ansteigenden Gatúnsee auf, ein Kranschiff findet den Weg zum Pazifik. An Bord der Ancon erleben Gäste die erste offizielle Durchfahrt. Ein Jahr später schicken abrutschende Hänge die Schiffe zurück.
summary.en: A tug climbs to the still-rising Gatún Lake. A crane boat reaches the Pacific. Passengers aboard Ancon witness the official opening. A year later the movement of the hills sends ships back the way they came.

“Panama Railroad at the Summit, 1855”, on the last rail laid 27 January and Robert Tomes’s account of buying oranges in the first year. Also “Barbacoas Bridge” and view of Front Street in Colón.

AA00016037/00001, scans image0003–image0004, ‘The Contest’ and ‘The Entries’, for the circular sent to fifteen newspapers, relief packages, posting deadline and anniversary. List of entrants on image0005 and image0007 includes Clarke and Simmons.

Modern American History 7 (1), pp. 127–130, especially pp. 127 and 130. The author identifies the 112 written testimonies in Box 25 of the Isthmian Historical Society collection at the Library of Congress and discusses how they were solicited and kept.

Printed pp. 107–108, Foreign Minister Solís on breaking relations. Pp. 109–112, Guevara Paz, “Relato objetivo de lo ocurrido en Balboa el jueves 9 de enero”, first published by La Estrella de Panamá, 14 January 1964. Includes Díaz, Gorgas Hospital, the delegation and the testimony attributed to Carranza.
Report of 9 January 2014. Identifies the Instituto Nacional flag, its custodians, movement to the Canal Museum in 2013, textile treatment in Spain and exhibition in the former Balboa school.
Paragraphs on the 1964 flag dispute, interruption and resumption of relations, and US Senate votes on the two treaties in 1978.
OpenStreetMap way 609527463, Centro de Capacitación Ascanio Arosemena. Building point for the former school identified in the ACP exhibition notice. The map does not place individual marchers.
FRUS, 1964–1968, volume XXXI, document 410, 3 April 1964, pp. 867–869. The presidents discuss restoring diplomatic relations, naming representatives and the absence of preconditions.
24 September 1965. Presidential statements issued in Washington and Panama City, especially point 1 of the joint statement on the replacement of the 1903 treaty.

22 October 2006. Ballot question, voting and turnout tables and project footnote. 705,284 yes, 201,105 no, 9,967 blank and 7,673 invalid; 924,029 ballots, 2,132,842 registered. The printed 76.3% uses all ballots. The yes/no subtotal of 906,389 gives 77.8% yes.

Title XV, Chapter 1, Article 325, first, third and fourth paragraphs. A proposal for a third set of locks requires executive and legislative approval, then a national referendum at least three months after legislative approval.

Section 5.6, pp. 47–48, fig. 32 and note 78, gravity, three basins per chamber, 60% reuse within the new system and projected 7% less water per transit than the old locks. Section 7, p. 53, proposal using existing reservoirs.

Report RL30981, updated 16 November 2006, pp. CRS-15–16, “Canal Expansion Project”. Torrijos on revenue for social programmes and the Coordinadora Campesina Contra los Embalses on the risk of displacement. These are arguments put forward during the campaign.

Spanish section, pp. 29–30, “Crónica de un día inolvidable”, arrivals by bus, crowd at noon, entry at about 3 p.m. and ship’s horn at Cocolí. P. 53, training and chartered Baroque. English section, p. 191, completed inauguration and more than 200 transits through September; p. 193, Baroque and Oceanus trials.

29 April 2016, paragraphs identifying the two participating lines and their ships Andronikos and Thalatta, the venue, the notary, Jorge Quijano, the drawing of the two names and the selected ship’s length and beam.

30 April 2016. Opening paragraphs describe the previous morning’s draw in the rotunda using the national lottery urn. Reporter names Margarita Azucena, notary Víctor Aldana Aparicio and administrator Jorge Quijano, and identifies both ships.
“Centro de Visitantes de Agua Clara – Gatún” and “Exhibición panorámica”. The public visitor site overlooks the Caribbean-side works near Colón.

National Archives Identifier 100997804, caption 311-A on the photograph. The dated print shows staff and workers at the pay car. The NARA/DPLA item record and US public-domain statement accompany the 1,761 × 1,443 pixel file.

Scribner’s Magazine 57 (4), April 1915, p. 396 (wage rolls and European labourers) and p. 404, photograph caption ‘Pay car at Culebra, January 12, 1908’: the carriage had counters and separate entrance and exit. This is an account by the former chief engineer and then governor.

AA00016037/00101, typescript pp. 1–3 (scan files image0029–image0031). Arrival by railway at San Pablo in 1908, coal and track work, father's referral, friends at Tabernilla, January 1910 move to the Gatún spillway, railway assignments and the concrete crane. labels.de: 1536 · Die Stadt Panamá baut ein Lagerhaus in Cruces
labels.en: 1536 · Panamá builds a warehouse at Cruces

summary.de: Am Río Chagres wechselte die Ladung zwischen den Lastkähnen und den Maultieren. Das städtische Lagerhaus von 1536 hatte 47 Kammern.
summary.en: Cargo switched between river craft and pack mules on the Chagres. The municipal warehouse built here in 1536 had forty-seven compartments.

labels.de: 28. Januar 1855 · Der erste Zug durchquert die Landenge
labels.en: 28 January 1855 · The first train crosses the isthmus

summary.de: Am 28. Januar 1855 fuhr der Eröffnungszug von Colón, auch Aspinwall genannt, nach Panamá. Die Strecke maß rund 76 Kilometer.
summary.en: On 28 January 1855 the inaugural train ran from Colón, also called Aspinwall, to Panamá. The line was 47.5 miles long.

labels.de: 29. Mai 1879 · Die Mehrheit stimmt für einen Kanal auf Meereshöhe
labels.en: 29 May 1879 · A majority votes for a sea-level canal

summary.de: Der Pariser Kongress zieht einen Durchstich in Panama dem Plan für einen Schleusenkanal und einer Route durch Nicaragua vor. Der Ingenieur Pedro Sosa aus Panama gehört zu den Befürwortern.
summary.en: In Paris the majority favours a sea-level cut in Panama. Delegates have also heard a lock proposal for Panama and a route through Nicaragua. Pedro Sosa of Panama supports the cut.

labels.de: September 1882 · Die Schwestern am Cerro Ancón
labels.en: September 1882 · The sisters on Ancón Hill

summary.de: Die französische Kanalgesellschaft eröffnete auf dem Hang ihr Zentralkrankenhaus. Die Schwestern vom heiligen Vinzenz von Paul empfingen dort auch Kranke aus den Stationen entlang der Kanalbaustellen.
summary.en: The French canal company opened its central hospital on the hill. The Sisters of St Vincent de Paul received patients referred by dispensaries along the excavations.

labels.de: 23. Januar 1905 · Wer in Bridgetown an Bord ging

summary.de: William J. Karner wirbt im Barbados Advocate um Arbeitskräfte für die Kanalbaukommission. Später erzählen Rückkehrer in den Dörfern von ihren Erfahrungen, und am Kai von Bridgetown verabschieden Familien die nächsten Reisenden.
summary.en: William J. Karner appeals for canal recruits in the Barbados Advocate. Men returning to the island share their experiences, and families gather at the Bridgetown wharf to see off those who follow.

labels.de: 1908 · Gatún räumt den Platz für den Damm
labels.en: 1908 · Gatún moves from the dam site

summary.de: Das Dorf am Fluss ist 1908 aufgegeben. Die meisten Gebäude stehen danach wieder in Nuevo Gatún. Fels und Erde des Damms bedecken den früheren Standort.
summary.en: The riverside village has been abandoned by 1908. Most of its buildings are re-erected at Nuevo Gatún. Earth and rock for the dam cover the old site.

labels.de: 15. August 1914 · Die Ancon auf der offiziellen Eröffnungsfahrt
labels.en: 15 August 1914 · Ancon on the official opening passage

summary.de: Der Lotse John A. Constantine führte den Dampfer von Cristóbal bis zu den äußeren pazifischen Fahrwassertonnen. Eine Aufnahme vom Cerro Luisa zeigt das Einlaufen in Pedro Miguel.
summary.en: The pilot John A. Constantine took the steamer from Cristóbal to the outer Pacific buoys. A photograph from Cerro Luisa shows it entering Pedro Miguel Locks.

labels.de: 31. Dezember 1999, 12 Uhr Ortszeit · Zwei Feiern und ein genauer Zeitpunkt
labels.en: 31 December 1999, noon Panama time · Two ceremonies and an hour set by treaty

summary.de: Vor dem Verwaltungsgebäude in Balboa zählt eine Uhr die Zeit bis zur Übergabe. Um zwölf Uhr mittags übernimmt Panama den Betrieb. Die internationale Feier in Miraflores lag bereits siebzehn Tage zurück.
summary.en: A clock outside the Administration Building in Balboa counts down to the handover. Panama takes over at noon, seventeen days after the international ceremony at Miraflores.

labels.de: 1. Oktober 2023 bis 30. September 2024 · Wenig Regen im Einzugsgebiet des Kanals
labels.en: 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024 · A rain shortage in the canal watershed

summary.de: Für das Geschäftsjahr 2023/24 verzeichnet die Kanalbehörde 2.118 Millimeter Regen im Einzugsgebiet und 542 Millionen Kubikmeter für Trinkwasser. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Gatúnsee. Die ESA-Aufnahmen stammen aus den Jahren vor der trockenen Regenzeit.
summary.en: For fiscal year 2023/24 the authority records 2,118 millimetres of rain across the watershed and 542 million cubic metres for drinking water. The point represents Gatún Lake. The ESA imagery predates the dry rainy season.

summary.de: Ein Magazin am Chagres, ein Lohnwagen und die Fahrt der Ancon erzählen, wer die Landenge überquerte und wer ihre Wasserwege schuf. Vom alten Gatún führt der Weg bis zur Übergabe an Panama und zur Dürre von 2023.
summary.en: A Chagres warehouse, a pay car and the voyage of the Ancon reveal who crossed the isthmus and who made its waterways. From old Gatún the guide follows the handover to Panama and the drought of 2023.

Figure 2, figure 3 and tables 1–2, pp. 129–134, locate the five grinding tools, stratigraphic contexts and thirteen grains identified as maize. Discussion of wild food and shellfish on pp. 137–139.
Sections 1.1–1.2 and figure 3. Coastal habitats, shellfish, sixth-century human remains, the Indigenous settlement at Morelos Park and instructions for Spanish port foundations.

Section 2, “Description and history”, opening discussion of the itineraries. Follow the sequence Nombre de Dios, coastal navigation, Chagres, Venta de Cruces and Panamá Viejo. The evaluation dates the village of Cruces to 1533, before the warehouse. Also the 1597 transfer and the relocation of Panamá in 1673.

Geographical data, component 1582rev-005, Archaeological Site of Panamá Viejo, 9°00′23.97″ N, 79°29′06.98″ W. General point for the site. Aceituno and Martín figure 2 locates the excavated square and neighbouring properties within it.

Anales del Museo de América XX, pp. 264–267, ports, the foundation of San Felipe de Portobelo, the fairs, merchandise and provisioning. Pp. 267–269, especially p. 268, the two itineraries, the municipal warehouse built at Cruces in 1536, 47 compartments, enslaved households, river transport and cargo craft.

Doctoral thesis, pp. 193–201 and figs. 15–26, survey near Nombre de Dios and ceramics of Lomita de Piedra. Section 5.1.1 on Luis de Mozambique. Conclusions 2–4, pp. 402–407, 1579 agreement, the rejected site, limited freedom, guarded coast, farm produce and the search for other fugitives.
TGN 7006459, inhabited place, coordinates 9.5790 N, 79.4710 W, and relationship to Santiago del Príncipe. The point marks the neighbouring port. The precise site of the maroon town remains uncertain.
Geographical data, component 135-001 Portobelo, 9°33′14″ N, 79°39′21″ W. Area of the harbour rather than an individual fair stall or berth.

Chapter II, pp. 11–17 in the 1857 edition: transfer at Gatún, steps, luggage, the reasons for hiring a private boat, fare, crew, hammock, poles, rising river and the butcher at Gorgona. The memoir looks back on the journey.

Caribbean workers on the Panama Canal, part 3 “Women in the Story”, p. 41. Dates Mary Seacole’s journey to Panama to 1851 and identifies her brother’s hotel. The date is not the publication date of her memoir.
GeoNames 3709287, Gatún Dam at 9.262778 N, 79.930000 W. Rounded modern reference for the former village site covered by the dam.
July 4, 1952, p. 6. Reprint of the December 6, 1911 account of the Chagres settlements. Passage on the old village of Gatun in the river flats, abandonment in 1908, and the site under Gatun Dam.

“Inversión extranjera y la construcción de la línea férrea”, passages on Manzanillo Island, the two port names, construction begun in 1850, 47.5 miles, the inauguration on 28 January 1855 and class fares. Later discussion of the French purchase of over 98% of railroad shares. DOI 10.18232/alhe.v22i2.588.
Chapter 2, “Migration to Panama in the 19th Century”, pp. 55–58. Origins of the railroad workforce and arrival of workers from China during construction.
“Panama Railroad at the Summit, 1855”, on the last rail laid 27 January and Robert Tomes’s account of buying oranges in the first year. Also “Barbacoas Bridge” and view of Front Street in Colón.
TGN 7006458, coordinates 9.3500 N, 79.9000 W, Aspinwall as alternative name, historical note on the northern terminus. City-level point on Manzanillo Island.

Smithsonian Libraries and Archives, BHL item 238774, single foldout map, compiled from the original surveys, 1857. Compare the Chagres, the railway alignment, and the track profile along the left edge. Item-level Copyright & Usage identifies the work as public domain; DOI 10.5962/bhl.title.140712.

“Textual description of the boundary of the nominated property”, components 002 and 003, Camino de Cruces sections 1 and 2. Section 2 begins at Venta de Cruces near the northern entrance to the Culebra Cut. Compare proposed site maps 04 and 05 and the distinct archaeological-site point for Panamá Viejo in the opening table.

Vol. XXVI, no. 7, 15 February 1855, third scanned page (leaf n2). Under ‘California’, the paragraph following the arrival of the steamships North Star and Prometheus reports that the first train ran from Aspinwall to Panama on 28 January.

Harper & Brothers, pp. 39–40. Otis describes the original railway from Manzanillo Island to Playa Prieta, the crossing at Barbacoas, the bends of the Chagres, the position of old Gorgona relative to the line and the ascent of the Río Obispo valley.

labels.de: Über die Landenge von Panama vor dem Kanalbau
labels.en: Crossing the Isthmus of Panama before the canal

labels.de: 15. August 1519 · Panamá entsteht auf einem älteren Siedlungsplatz
labels.en: 15 August 1519 · Panamá is founded on an older settlement

summary.de: Am späteren Hauptplatz sind indigene und koloniale Schichten erhalten. Mahlsteine aus den frühen Stadthäusern tragen Spuren von Mais.
summary.en: Indigenous and colonial deposits survive at the later main square. Grinding tools from early colonial properties carry traces of maize.

labels.de: 1536 · Die Stadt Panamá baut ein Lagerhaus in Cruces
labels.en: 1536 · Panamá builds a warehouse at Cruces

summary.de: Am Río Chagres wechselte die Ladung zwischen den Lastkähnen und den Maultieren. Das städtische Lagerhaus von 1536 hatte 47 Kammern.
summary.en: Cargo switched between river craft and pack mules on the Chagres. The municipal warehouse built here in 1536 had forty-seven compartments.

labels.de: 1579 · Eine Gemeinde erkämpft sich anerkannte Freiheit
labels.en: 1579 · A community wins recognition of its freedom

summary.de: Die Gemeinschaft um Luis de Mozambique handelte die Anerkennung ihrer Freiheit aus und siedelte bei Nombre de Dios. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Nachbarhafen, die Lage von Santiago del Príncipe ist nur ungefähr bekannt.
summary.en: Luis de Mozambique’s community negotiated recognition of its freedom and settled near Nombre de Dios. The marker locates the neighbouring port. The site of Santiago del Príncipe is uncertain.

labels.de: 20. März 1597 · San Felipe de Portobelo wird gegründet
labels.en: 20 March 1597 · Foundation of San Felipe de Portobelo

summary.de: Die spanische Krone verlegte den karibischen Hafen von Nombre de Dios nach Portobelo. Zur Zeit der Messen verteuerten sich Lebensmittel, Unterkünfte und Lagerraum.
summary.en: Spain transferred its Caribbean port from Nombre de Dios to Portobelo. The fairs drove up the cost of provisions, rooms and storage.

labels.de: 1851 · Mary Seacole wechselt in Gatún vom Zug aufs Boot
labels.en: 1851 · Mary Seacole transfers from train to boat at Gatún

summary.de: In ihrer Autobiografie schildert Seacole die Fahrt nach Cruces. Vier Männer paddelten oder stakten, der Bootsführer steuerte, und Hochwasser zwang sie zu einer Übernachtung.
summary.en: In her memoir Seacole describes the trip to Cruces. Four men paddled and poled, the master steered, and high water forced an overnight stop.

labels.de: 28. Januar 1855 · Der erste Zug durchquert die Landenge
labels.en: 28 January 1855 · The first train crosses the isthmus

summary.de: Am 28. Januar 1855 fuhr der Eröffnungszug von Colón, auch Aspinwall genannt, nach Panamá. Die Strecke maß rund 76 Kilometer.
summary.en: On 28 January 1855 the inaugural train ran from Colón, also called Aspinwall, to Panamá. The line was 47.5 miles long.

summary.de: Mahlsteine unter dem Hauptplatz von Panamá, die Freiheit einer Gemeinde bei Nombre de Dios und Mary Seacoles Bootsfahrt erzählen vom Leben entlang der Wege. 1855 verband erstmals ein Zug die beiden Küsten.
summary.en: Grinding tools from Panamá, a maroon settlement near Nombre de Dios and Mary Seacole’s boat journey reveal the work of crossing the isthmus. In 1855 a train linked the two coasts.

France, instruction of 25 April designating Daniel Ammen and civil engineer Menocal. The paragraph defining the non-official character of the congress limits their participation to discussion by experts.

Address in the site footer and map link for the museum on Plaza de la Independencia. The destination marker is at 8.9520349, −79.5346031, rounded here for the former company building.

labels.en: The French canal project in Panama

labels.de: 18. Mai 1878 · Kolumbien setzt die geänderte Konzession in Kraft
labels.en: 18 May 1878 · Colombia enacts the amended concession

summary.de: Julián Trujillo setzt Gesetz 28 in Kraft. Wyse nimmt die Änderungen an dem Vertrag an, den er mit Eustorgio Salgar ausgehandelt hatte.
summary.en: Julián Trujillo enacts Law 28. Wyse accepts the amendments to the agreement he had negotiated with Eustorgio Salgar.

labels.de: 29. Mai 1879 · Die Mehrheit stimmt für einen Kanal auf Meereshöhe
labels.en: 29 May 1879 · A majority votes for a sea-level canal

summary.de: Der Pariser Kongress zieht einen Durchstich in Panama dem Plan für einen Schleusenkanal und einer Route durch Nicaragua vor. Der Ingenieur Pedro Sosa aus Panama gehört zu den Befürwortern.
summary.en: In Paris the majority favours a sea-level cut in Panama. Delegates have also heard a lock proposal for Panama and a route through Nicaragua. Pedro Sosa of Panama supports the cut.

labels.de: 8.–9. Dezember 1880 · Die Gesellschaft bietet ihre Aktien an
labels.en: 8–9 December 1880 · The company offers its shares to the public

summary.de: 590.000 Aktien stehen bei der öffentlichen Zeichnung zum Nennwert von je 500 Francs bereit. Das erhaltene Stück trägt die Nummer 278792.
summary.en: The public offering comprises 590,000 shares with a face value of 500 francs each. The surviving certificate pictured here is number 278792.

labels.de: Juli 1886 · Ein neuer Bauvertrag für Culebra
labels.en: July 1886 · A new contract for work at Culebra

summary.de: Artigue, Sonderegger et Cie. übernimmt Arbeiten im Einschnitt. Die Mannschaften müssen dem Hang Boden abgewinnen und den Aushub so weit abfahren, dass er auch bei Regen liegen bleibt.
summary.en: Artigue, Sonderegger et Cie. takes on work at the cut. Crews have to excavate the hillsides and carry the spoil far enough away to keep it out of the channel during the rains.

labels.de: 4. Februar 1889 · Das Gericht ordnet die Liquidation an

summary.de: Das Pariser Zivilgericht setzt einen Liquidator ein. Am Isthmus laufen einzelne Arbeiten noch bis zum 15. Mai.
summary.en: The civil court in Paris appoints a liquidator. Some work on the isthmus continues until 15 May.

labels.de: 4. Mai 1904 · Die Schlüssel wechseln den Besitzer

summary.de: Im ehemaligen Grand Hôtel nimmt Mark Brooke die französischen Anlagen auf dem Isthmus für die USA in Empfang. Er bestätigt die Übergabe in drei Sprachen.
summary.en: In the former Grand Hôtel, Mark Brooke accepts the French company property on the isthmus for the United States. He records the handover in three languages.

summary.de: Kolumbien vergibt eine Konzession. In Paris stimmen Fachleute über die Höhe des Wassers ab, in Bayonne bezahlt jemand eine Aktie in Raten. Bei Culebra entscheidet der Abtransport des Aushubs mit über das Schicksal des Kanals.
summary.en: Colombia grants a concession. Delegates in Paris vote on the height of the water, and someone in Bayonne pays for a share by instalments. At Culebra the work of hauling spoil helps decide the canal’s fate.

Sections on Colombia’s rejection of the Hay–Herrán Treaty, the November independence movement, US naval support and Bunau-Varilla’s engineering and diplomatic roles.

Sie führte südlich am alten Gorgona vorbei und stieg im Tal des Río Obispo zur Wasserscheide bei Culebra an.
note.en: On 28 January 1855 the first through passenger train ran from Colón (Aspinwall) on the Atlantic to Playa Prieta in Panama City on the Pacific. The railway crossed the Chagres at Barbacoas, passed south of old Gorgona and climbed the Río Obispo valley to the divide at Culebra.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 November 2021, “Antecedentes históricos” and “Antes de la segunda guerra mundial”: September 1882 opening, choice of the slope of Cerro Ancón to catch breezes away from city wastewater, US acquisition and reuse of the grounds. note.en: The French canal company opened its central hospital on the hill. The Sisters of St Vincent de Paul received patients referred by dispensaries along the excavations.

sourceRefs.locator: Societas 19 (1), 73–91, printed p. 78. Paragraph immediately preceding “El puerto de La Boca – Balboa”: engineers’ selection of the old French reservoir on the upper Río Grande and water running through Panama City’s mains on 4 July 1905.

Passages following the reorganization under David H. Brandon. The hydrant system was inaugurated in Cathedral Square on 4 July 1905. At the Malambo fire of 12 January 1906 the firefighters used pumps connected to cisterns.

Printed pp. 178–179, paragraph beginning “Uno de tales proyectos”: the Star and Herald / La Estrella called for water mains in the 1880s for drinking water and fire protection and reported on the municipal water contract in 1888.

1 May 2024, opening four paragraphs, fig. 1 and Main findings. May–December 2023 rainfall near the Gatún catchment, lake levels, ship number and size restrictions, rising urban demand and leakage, influence of El Niño, differing station trends and insufficient evidence for attribution of observed drying to human-caused warming.

note.de: In Panama-Stadt floss Wasser aus dem oberen Río Grande durch die neuen Leitungen. Die Feuerwehr überliefert die Einweihung der Hydranten auf dem Kathedralplatz und einen späteren Brand, bei dem sie noch Zisternen nutzte.
note.en: Water from the upper Río Grande entered Panama City’s new mains. The fire brigade records the opening of the hydrant system in Cathedral Square and a subsequent fire at which it still used cisterns.

note.en: The line follows the outward voyage of the Ancon on 15 August 1914. From Cristóbal the ship went by Gatún, Gamboa, Culebra Cut, Pedro Miguel and Miraflores, passing Balboa on its way into the Pacific. It then returned to Balboa to disembark its passengers.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 November 2021, “Antecedentes históricos” and “Antes de la segunda guerra mundial”: September 1882 opening, choice of the slope of Cerro Ancón to catch breezes away from city wastewater, US acquisition and reuse of the grounds. MINSA gives 12 September for the opening. The thanksgiving Mass is separately dated to the 17th by Escobar. The station therefore identifies the opening by month.

Chapter VI, “Hospitales en la Época del Canal Francés”, pp. CXLIX–CLI. Companyo, his earlier work at Suez, Huerta de Gallo, the fundraising committee, the September thanksgiving Mass, transfers of patients, the sisters, Colón, the former Taboga hotel and the orphanage. Chapter VII, pp. CLXXIV–CLXXVI, reports the 1916 request for larger premises and lottery funding. Pp. CLXXXII–CLXXXIII name the four nursing graduates of 1912. For the 1924 opening date use the contemporary decrees, which supersede the December date printed on p. CLXXV.

Public Health Reports 19 (8), 19 February 1904, printed p. 277, “Hospitals”: wooden, separated pavilions of the French hospital, nursing by Sisters of Charity, twenty-four patients in the foreign section and twenty in the canal section. This is a count made before the US canal administration assumed the hospital.

“Gustave Eiffel”, final paragraphs on the first canal company, receivership and the appointment of a liquidator. Escobar, pp. CL–CLI, traces how the breakdown of the construction enterprise affected its hospitals.

Ficha P1405, Antiguo Hospital Gorgas, Calle Gorgas y Calle Juan de Arco Galindo, Ancón, records 659775.38 E, 990772.36 N in WGS84 / UTM zone 17N, converted to 8.96024° N, 79.54667° W. Marks the hospital complex as rebuilt from 1915 to 1919. For the continuity of the French hospital site see Escobar, p. CXLIX, and MINSA. Individual wards and earlier pavilions are not fixed by this point.

Chapter XVI, “Malaria Work and the Hospital System”, printed p. 226, paragraph beginning “The nursing force was composed”. Gorgas describes the Black maids and orderlies who worked in the French hospital, including direct care and manual work under the sisters’ supervision.
Ficha P1405. Hospital complex on the site of Huerta de Gallo. Modern orientation point for the grounds, not the footprint of a particular French pavilion.

sourceRefs.locator: New West Indian Guide 59 (1–2), pp. 1–26. Bridgetown wharf, lighters, Carlisle Bay and the distinction between contracted and noncontract migrants appear on pp. 9–10.

Workforce recruitment, from the paragraph beginning ‘It was recognized early on’ through the separate discussions of Barbados and Jamaica. The figure of 19,900 is recruitment in Barbados. Jamaica refused recruiting and required intending emigrants to cover tax and passage. Skilled workers were among those able to pay.

23 March 2016. Paragraphs describing two training lakes, a reproduction of Culebra Cut, the 1:25 models used by pilots and tug captains, the Maersk Edinburgh model, and wave and wind generators.

Spanish section, pp. 29–30, “Crónica de un día inolvidable”, arrivals by bus, crowd at noon, entry at about 3 p.m. and ship’s horn at Cocolí. P. 53, training and chartered Baroque. Approximate former settlement shown west of the canal on Annex 4, figure 1. The 1906 minutes locate the chief engineer's office in Culebra on the date of his letter; they do not identify the building in which it was written.

May–December 2023 rainfall near the Gatún catchment, lake levels, ship number and size restrictions, rising urban demand and leakage, influence of El Niño, differing station trends and insufficient evidence for attribution of observed drying to human-caused warming.

PDF p. 1. The fishery authority gives 09°10′31.7″ N, 79°54′06.4″ W as a representative location for the lake. Watershed totals are regional.

Cuadernos Nacionales 37, pp. 151–154, section “Estación de Gatún.” Figures 32 and 36 locate the original and relocated railway station and relate the latter to the buildings and shoreline. Figure 33 and the text on pp. 152–153 describe the platform, ticket office, telegraph and baggage room.

Memoria del Hospital Santo Tomás 2020–2021, “Recordar es vivir”, caption and opening paragraph. The institution identifies the ceremony and the inauguration by President Belisario Porras on 1 September 1924.

Chapter VI, “Hospitales en la Época del Canal Francés”, pp. CXLIX–CLI. Companyo, his earlier work at Suez, Huerta de Gallo, the fundraising committee, the September thanksgiving Mass, transfers of patients, the sisters, Colón, the former Taboga hotel and the orphanage. processingNote.de: Die Linie folgt der Hinfahrt der Ancon am 15. August 1914. Von Cristóbal führte sie über Gatún, Gamboa, den Culebra-Einschnitt, Pedro Miguel und Miraflores an Balboa vorbei bis auf den Pazifik. Anschließend kehrte der Dampfer zur Ausschiffung nach Balboa zurück.

sourceRefs.locator: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 719, pp. 707–708. Enclosure is dated 20 January, cover letter 24 January, supplementary note 25 January. Eighteen official reports since 1 July 1904 included the four sanitary labourers still in hospital on 20 January. Three deaths, the cities and intervening zone, bills of health for shipping and the reported recoveries appear in the circular and note.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 718, pp. 706–707, especially enclosure 2, the translated reply of Panama’s minister of government and foreign affairs, 21 January 1905. De la Guardia explains his authorization and the changes suggested by his office when accepting the sanitary regulations under article VII.

Doctoral thesis, printed p. 50, citing Rodríguez on the 1904 appointment and 1908 count of 117 nurses among 205 US women employed in the Canal Zone. Note 49 quotes La Estrella de Panamá, 9 February 1905, vol. LVI, no. 13544, p. 10, on malaria admissions and the latrines at Ancón. Pp. 52–53 quote the same newspaper of 13 March 1909 on admission of single women aged sixteen to twenty-five at Santo Tomás.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 723, enclosure 2, paragraph beginning “Immediately after seeing”. Barrett locates the legation near the corner of the canal building and the Plaza. The square serves only to orient the January circular in the capital. Its text gives no legation street address.

June 2022 table, region 2, entry no. 788, Plaza de La Catedral, San Felipe, 8.95276° N, 79.53502° W. Square-level location. For the January circular the square is an orientation point near the contemporary legation. The July hydrant ceremony is explicitly placed in the square by the Panamanian fire brigade.

RNI 2.0, entry 788. According to Barrett’s 8 May letter, the American legation was near the plaza and the canal building. The point represents the neighborhood, not a diplomatic office or the four patients’ ward.

Section 5.6, pp. 47–48, fig. 32 and note 78, gravity, three basins per chamber, 60% reuse within the new system and projected 7% less water per transit than the old locks. Section 7, p. 53, proposal using existing reservoirs.

The editorial assessment of the losses occurs on p. 120.

sourceRefs.locator: Smithsonian Libraries and Archives, BHL item 238774, single foldout map, compiled from the original surveys, 1857. Compare the Chagres, the railway alignment, and the track profile along the left edge. Item-level Copyright & Usage identifies the work as public domain; DOI 10.5962/bhl.title.140712.
“Panama Railroad at the Summit, 1855”, on the last rail laid 27 January and Robert Tomes’s account of buying oranges in the first year. Also “Barbacoas Bridge” and view of Front Street in Colón.

“Inversión extranjera y la construcción de la línea férrea”, passages on Manzanillo Island, the two port names, construction begun in 1850, 47.5 miles, the inauguration on 28 January 1855 and class fares. TGN 7006458, coordinates 9.3500 N, 79.9000 W, Aspinwall as alternative name, historical note on the northern terminus. City-level point on Manzanillo Island.

Vol. XXVI, no. 7, 15 February 1855, third scanned page (leaf n2). Under ‘California’, the paragraph following the arrival of the steamships North Star and Prometheus reports that the first train ran from Aspinwall to Panama on 28 January.

Harper & Brothers, pp. 39–40. Otis describes the original railway from Manzanillo Island to Playa Prieta, the crossing at Barbacoas, the bends of the Chagres, the position of old Gorgona relative to the line and the ascent of the Río Obispo valley.

note.de: Die Linie folgt Thomas Harrisons Karte von 1857. Die Punkte sind auf 0,01° gerundet. Zwischen ihnen sind Gleisbögen und Flussquerungen nur im Kilometermaßstab dargestellt.
note.en: The line follows Thomas Harrison’s 1857 map. Points are rounded to 0.01°. The curves and river crossings between them are approximate at kilometre scale.

processingNote.de: Am 28. Januar 1855 fuhr der erste durchgehende Personenzug von Colón (Aspinwall) am Atlantik nach Playa Prieta in Panama-Stadt am Pazifik. Bei Barbacoas überquerte die Bahn den Chagres. Sie führte südlich am alten Gorgona vorbei und stieg im Tal des Río Obispo zur Wasserscheide bei Culebra an.
processingNote.en: On 28 January 1855 the first through passenger train ran from Colón (Aspinwall) on the Atlantic to Playa Prieta in Panama City on the Pacific. The railway crossed the Chagres at Barbacoas, passed south of old Gorgona and climbed the Río Obispo valley to the divide at Culebra.
